newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Russia, U.S. agree on nuclear disarmament steps.
newsitem.headline: Russia, U.S. agree on nuclear disarmament steps.

text.p: Russia and the United States agreed late on Tuesday on practical steps to begin inspecting the Russian Federation's nuclear arsenal, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said on Wednesday.

U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary and Russian Federation Atomic Energy Minister Viktor Mikhailov, meeting at the IAEA's annual congress, had agreed to step up technical cooperation in line with the 1995 nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, it said.
"This is a further step towards an inspection system of nuclear weapons and equipping the Russians with the technology for that," IAEA spokesman Hans Meyer told Reuters.
He said the Russian Federation had agreed to place fissile material -- uranium and plutonium stocks -- under IAEA inspection, but the amount had not been specified.
O'Leary told the congress the United States had already placed 200 tonnes of nuclear material under the agency's inspection since 1993 and would designate 26 more tonnes over the next three years.
Under the agreement, a Russian team will visit three nuclear stockpile sites in the United States to examine current safeguards with a view to implementing these in Russia.
The two countries also agreed to work together to protect sensitive information on nuclear weapons, the IAEA said.
The agreement follows guidelines agreed by President Bill Clinton and President Boris Yeltsin at meetings in 1994 and 1995.
